items.title: Distributed Ray Tracer
items.titleZh: 分布式光线追踪器
items.summary:
Hey HN, I'm Julius, I'm a backend engineer at Hatchet and created this demo to show off some of Hatchet's new features, primarily durable streams and serverless endpoints. Those, however, are just background details that made this significantly easier to scale. By distributing the rendering across many different nodes, orchestrated using Hatchet, it makes it possible to render quite high fidelity scenes fairly quickly. All of this would be possible on a single machine, but would be much slower without dedicated hardware (RT cores, etc). The renderer itself is using well-known ray tracing techniques, with no special considerations there. The renderer is a slightly modified version of https://github.com/ekzhang/rpt , with additional support for SDF scripting using https://docs.rs/fidget/latest/fidget/ . SDFs have been popular in the demoscene community, though perhaps not super well known outside of that, and are capable of creating some fantastic looking scenes: https://www.shadertoy.com/view/ld3Gz2 . The coolest part here is using a DSL to represent the SDFs in a rendering pipeline, and using LLMs with a chat interface to create them. The source is available here: https://github.com/hatchet-dev/distributed-ray-tracer

items.title: Show HN: Kapso – Iterative learning from enterprise data
items.titleZh: Show HN：Kapso – 从企业数据中迭代学习
items.summary: Hey HN! We're Alireza and Majid building Leeroo ( https://leeroo.com/ ). Previously we’ve built AI systems for products with millions of users, including at LinkedIn and Meta. We’re now focusing on building AI systems for enterprise data. Today, we're open-sourcing Kapso ( https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso ), an engine that runs experiments, deploys the best solution, and learns from every run. The nature of data work is iterative: investigate, form hypotheses, experiment, and improve based on what you learn. This bottom-up process is the only way to deliver meaningful outcomes quickly in large, messy enterprise data environments. Consultants gathering context in meetings or teams defining a business ontology upfront to fit into the data has no chance of execution, in quarters and sometimes years. An AI-native system should automate this process, compounding learning to each new investigation and implementation. For instance, one of our enterprise projects was moving a company off its old data estate onto a lakehouse with more than 30 source-system families, thousands of tables and transformations, and hundreds of BI reports. No individual or AI agent knew how that data estate was connected and operated. The only way to learn it was to investigate the company's repos, dbt models, documentation, and data itself and propose hypotheses about the estate, run experiments, and learn from them, until we understand how each system behaves and under which conditions. The iterative work goes beyond understanding how data and systems fit together, and the business operations. Building useful software is iterative too. Whether you’re optimizing a warehouse, building a lakehouse pipeline or predicting churn, you need to run experiments and learn what works best in that environment. As you deliver more projects, that know-how compounds, similar in principle to RL. RAGing documentation has little value until it has been tried in a specific environment and the consequences are learned. As with human engineering work, experimentation and learning should happen in a sandbox. We built Kapso for this kind of work, you give it an objective and success criteria, and it works towards an optimum solution that can be deployed on your stack. You can view a video walkthrough here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W4FHlza1fRs Here’s how it works… Kapso has a bank of lessons that are induced or deduced from the past experiments, and each carries a credence score, conditions on where it applies, and the evidence behind it. For each new experiment, an ideation module proposes ideas considering the earlier lessons, re-ranks them by expected return against the budget each would use, and sends the top-ranked ones to the implementor. Because the bank keeps learning from the past experiments in that environment, the proposed ideas are better suited to it than generic hypotheses from an LLM or RAG. Also, results of each experiment are verified by a verifier module that no experiment can access and cheat. As we’ve found when building such systems, sometimes the success criteria and evaluation tests need to be evolved. The experimentation modules can propose updates to the metrics and criteria for the verifier to approve or reject. After each run, learn() updates the bank of lessons’ scores and boundaries using the evidence from that run. Changes to the bank can also be A/B tested by running otherwise identical builds with the previous and updated banks. The bank is built on git, so you can share your experience with others, list the banks available to you, and update them (`kapso experience share/list/update` in CLI). The system is model-agnostic and coding-agent-agnostic. kapso.deploy(solution, target_stack) follows the same workflow, runs a shorter experimentation loop to adapt the best solution to the target stack (e.g. Docker, Modal, BentoCloud, LangGraph). Every domain has a harness to start from, you can write your own domain harness with /kapso:harness in t
items.summaryZh: 嘿，HN！我们是 Alireza 和 Majid，正在构建 Leeroo ( https://leeroo.com/ )。此前，我们已经为拥有数百万用户的产品构建了人工智能系统，包括 LinkedIn 和 Meta。我们现在专注于为企业数据构建人工智能系统。今天，我们开源 Kapso ( https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso )，这是一个运行实验、部署最佳解决方案并从每次运行中学习的引擎。数据工作的本质是迭代：调查、形成假设、实验并根据所学进行改进。这种自下而上的流程是在大型、混乱的企业数据环境中快速交付有意义的结果的唯一方法。顾问在会议或团队中收集上下文，预先定义业务本体以适应数据，但在几个季度甚至几年内没有执行的机会。人工智能原生系统应该自动化这一过程，将学习与每项新的调查和实施相结合。例如，我们的一个企业项目是将一家公司从其旧数据资产迁移到拥有 30 多个源系统系列、数千个表和转换以及数百份 BI 报告的 LakeHouse。没有个人或人工智能代理知道数据资产是如何连接和操作的。了解它的唯一方法是调查公司的存储库、dbt 模型、文档和数据本身，并提出有关资产的假设、进行实验并从中学习，直到我们了解每个系统的行为方式以及在什么条件下。迭代工作超出了理解数据和系统如何组合以及业务运营的范围。构建有用的软件也是迭代的。无论您是优化仓库、构建 Lakehouse 管道还是预测客户流失，您都需要进行实验并了解在该环境中最有效的方法。随着您交付的项目越来越多，这些专业知识就会不断复合，原则上与强化学习类似。在特定环境中进行尝试并了解后果之前，RAGing 文档几乎没有任何价值。与人类工程工作一样，实验和学习应该在沙箱中进行。我们为此类工作构建了 Kapso，您给它一个目标和成功标准，它就会致力于提供可部署在您的堆栈上的最佳解决方案。您可以在这里观看视频演练：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W4FHlza1fRs 这是它的工作原理……卡普索有一系列从过去的实验中归纳或推导出来的经验教训，每个经验教训都带有一个信用分数，以及我在哪里的条件。
